svg.title: Figure 3. Measuring shear strain, and shearing stress across the width
svg.desc: Two panels. (a) A square element in pure shear distorts into a rhombus; one diagonal lengthens and the other shortens by half the shear strain, so a pair of gages at plus and minus 45 degrees measures the shear strain as the difference of their readings, and the axial strain from bending cancels. (b) Shearing stress on the neutral axis divided by the elementary value VQ over Ib, plotted across the width of rectangles with b over h of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 for Poisson's ratio 0.3: narrow sections are nearly uniform, but as the section gets wider the stress rises at the faces and falls at the center while its average stays equal to the elementary value.
